name: Science, Policy and Environment
description: An evidence-centered blueprint for research, public policy, institutions, scientific claims, and environmental systems.

guidance: Define the scientific or policy question, system boundary, population or geography, time horizon, stakeholders, and decision criterion.
Separate empirical observations, experimental or model results, assumptions, expert judgment, institutional position, value choice, and recommendation.
Evaluate methods, measurement, sampling, uncertainty, sensitivity, replication, and external validity before interpreting findings.
For policy, distinguish goals, instruments, implementation mechanisms, distributional effects, trade-offs, and evaluation criteria.
For environmental systems, preserve spatial scale, temporal scale, baselines, units, feedbacks, thresholds, and scenario assumptions.
Use charts only when scales, units, populations, and comparison bases are defensible; show uncertainty when supplied.
State contested evidence, knowledge gaps, governance constraints, and who bears costs or benefits.

sections.title: Question, Scope and Evidence-Supported Answer
sections.purpose: Define the research or policy question and answer it at the level supported by the available evidence.

blocks.title: Study, System and Policy Profile
instructions: State question, system boundary, population or geography, period, method or policy setting, evidence types, and material scope gaps.

blocks.title: Evidence-Supported Answer
instructions: Answer the objective with the central finding, confidence, mechanism or policy relevance, key trade-off, and most important uncertainty.
Distinguish observed result, modeled result, institutional claim, and normative judgment.

blocks.title: Key Findings and Policy Signals
instructions: Present distinct findings about magnitude, mechanism, heterogeneity, threshold, implementation, distribution, or uncertainty with scale and evidence locations.

sections.title: Methods, Evidence Quality and Mechanisms
sections.purpose: Explain how the evidence was produced, what mechanism it supports, and how design choices affect confidence.

blocks.title: Method and Mechanism Analysis
instructions: Analyze design, measurement, sampling, model structure, assumptions, uncertainty, sensitivity, causal identification, and external validity where available.
Do not upgrade correlation, simulation, or expert judgment into experimental evidence.

blocks.title: Evidence-to-Impact Pathway
instructions: Map one supported pathway from driver or intervention through mechanism and implementation to outcome; mark modeled, assumed, and observed links.

sections.title: Policy Options, System Effects and Trade-offs
sections.purpose: Compare plausible actions or interpretations across effectiveness, feasibility, distribution, timing, and unintended effects.

blocks.title: Options and System Trade-offs
instructions: Compare goals, instruments, mechanisms, stakeholders, implementation constraints, costs, benefits, time horizons, feedbacks, and distributional effects only where evidenced.
Separate empirical prediction from value choice.

blocks.title: Comparable Scientific or Policy Evidence

chart_slot.intent: Support one scientific or policy claim with comparable observations, scenarios, distributions, or trends.

fallback.message: No comparable quantitative scientific or policy evidence is available.

instructions: Preserve units, spatial and temporal scales, baselines, population, scenario labels, and uncertainty; never mix observed and modeled series without explicit distinction.

sections.title: Evidence Trail and Decision Implications
sections.purpose: Make claims auditable and translate the evidence into conditional, monitorable implications.

blocks.title: Evidence and Assumption Trail
instructions: Tie findings to methods, measurements, estimates, assumptions, scenarios, policy texts, stakeholder evidence, and exact locations.

blocks.title: Conditional Policy or Research Options
instructions: State the objective served, evidence basis, prerequisites, implementation risk, distributional concern, and evaluation indicator for each option.

sections.title: Uncertainty, Contestation and Knowledge Gaps
sections.purpose: State which methodological, system, governance, or value uncertainties could alter the conclusion.

blocks.title: Limitations and Open Questions
instructions: Identify material gaps in methods, measurement, uncertainty, sensitivity, external validity, spatial or temporal coverage, model assumptions, stakeholder representation, implementation, governance, or normative criteria.
